title: Vasquez's ground: no irrational thing is capable of honor per se—alone-adoration risks idolatry
source_text: LII. Fundamentum autem sententiae ejus est quod nulla res inanima, aut irrationalis sine rationali, capax est secundum se honoris, cultus, & reverentiae, seu adorationis. Et hoc quia adoratio est voluntas exhibendi alicui excellenti notam, & signum submissionis, excellentiae ipsius debitum: Jam vero animus submissionis, & servitutis erga illum ipsum versatur, quem quis apprehendit, ut sibi superiorem, & excellentia majori praeditum, qualis respectu hominis non est imago sine exemplari considerata. Ut pluribus exponit ipse disputationis jam dictae capite nono. ubi etiam affirmat, illum qui imaginem per se, non adorato in ipsa exemplari, veneratur, stultitiae, seu idololatriae infimulari posse: aut quia rei irrationali se subjicit, & contra rectam rationem se servum exhibet: aut quia dum illi se submittit, aliquod numen, aut dignitatem, aut virtutem ei tribuit; quod est error gentilium, non Christianorum religio.
pass_a_gloss: But the foundation of his opinion is that no inanimate thing, or irrational without a rational, is capable according to itself of honor, cult, and reverence, or adoration. And this because adoration is the will of exhibiting to someone excellent a mark and sign of submission owed to his excellence: But the mind of submission and of servitude is conversant toward that very one whom someone apprehends as superior to himself and endowed with greater excellence, of which sort, with respect to man, the image considered without the exemplar is not. As he himself explains at more length in chapter nine of the disputation already named. where he also affirms that he who venerates the image per se, the exemplar in it not being adored, can be charged with folly, or with idolatry: either because he subjects himself to an irrational thing and against right reason exhibits himself as a servant; or because while he submits himself to it he attributes to it some deity, or dignity, or virtue; which is the error of the Gentiles, not the religion of Christians.
pass_b_english: Vasquez's ground: nothing irrational is capable of honor per se, because adoration is willed submission to a superior excellence.
Image-alone veneration can be branded folly or idolatry—servitude to the irrational, or attributing deity or dignity to it (Gentile error, not Christian religion).

lemmas.gloss: is capable according to itself of honor
